originalTitle: Trump blasts appeals court for halting White House ballroom construction, claiming decision is a ‘national security threat’ – live
summary: President criticizes judges on social media after ruling puts two-week hold on controversial project
content: Donald Trump called the decision to halt construction of his $400m White House ballroom a “National Security Threat at the highest level” in a post on Truth Social. “We are not tenants, who pay rent and do all other things that a tenant must do, we are PRESIDENTS, elected by the people of the United States of America, and have many rights, including the right to fix, renovate, secure, protect, and beautify the White House grounds,” Trump wrote. “This decision, made after much of the work has been done and paid for, is a National Security Threat at the highest level.” Earlier today, a US federal appeals court sided with historic preservationists who sued to stop construction of the 90,000-square-foot (8,400-square-meter) ballroom, which he has repeatedly labeled as “a gift” to the US people. The order upheld a preliminary injunction won by the National Trust for Historic ⁠Preservation. The group sued last year after the Trump administration tore down the historic East Wing and began building a ballroom without seeking authorization from Congress. The appeals court put ⁠its ruling on hold for two weeks to allow the administration to appeal to the US supreme court. District court judge Richard Leon had said in a March opinion that any construction work left incomplete, although it poses concerns regarding the “safety and security of the White House grounds and the President himself, the existence of a ‘large hole’ beside the White House is, of course, a problem of the President’s own making.” A federal prosecutor fired last year over critical comments he had written as a private citizen about Donald Trump sued the justice department, the AP reports, saying his termination violated his first amendment rights. Will Rosenzweig was two weeks away from trying a multimillion-dollar Medicare fraud case when a blog he had written years earlier covering a broad range of topics was publicized online by a conservative political commentator who also included a screenshot of Rosenzweig’s LinkedIn account and tagged senior justice department officials for their awareness. Less than three hours after the post, the lawsuit says, Rosenzweig received an email signed by then attorney general Pam Bondi informing him that he had been fired. The news came as Rosenzweig was out of town with his family observing the Jewish holiday of Rosh Hashana. Oregon’s Democratic governor, Tina Kotek, said she supports locally set moratoriums on new data center construction, with her comments coming nearly two weeks after the city of Hillsboro became the first in the state to enact such a temporary prohibition. “Data center corporations are taking Oregon out to an expensive dinner and leaving our environment, communities, and people to foot the bill,” Kotek said in a statement. “Local governments are doing the right thing in calling for a pause until we can get this right.” Kotek also directed the department of administrative services last week to terminate Oregon’s contract for the sale of approximately 32 acres in southeast Salem for a proposed data center project. Her remarks respond to increasing concerns over data centers’ impacts on the environment and the electrical grid. A poll released this week found that 71% of Oregonians “have a negative impression of data centers.” Oregon currently has about 135 operational and planned data centers, according to Data Center Map. Donald Trump announced a list of deals and investments that aim to bolster mining, totaling more than $2 billion in projects and mining school investments. The largest chunk will go to the California-based company Sila Nanotechnologies to build a battery facility and expand production, coming as a $1.4b investment from the defense department. The department will also give $400m to Sunrise Energy Metals to develop scandium, which is used in fighter jets and spacecraft, among other companies. The Export-Import Bank, which provides financing to support US exports, is also investing in a boron deposit, battery manufacturing, and tantalum and niobium to make electronics, magnet, and steel. Donald Trump once again targeted Jeanine Pirro, the US attorney for the District of Columbia, this time writing a post on Truth Social saying she should “re-visit her hastily made decision” after she dismissed vandalism charges against Olympic canoeist David Hearn last week. Trump reposted images from a photographer of what seemed like the reflecting pool showing “slashes”, according to the US president, who also claimed “there were witnesses to the VANDALISM.” “U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro should re-visit her hastily made decision,” he wrote. These comments are just the latest in a series of snubs against Pirro, a longtime Trump ally. After her decision to dismiss the charges, the president accused her of having “folded like an umbrella.” He also told NBC News that he didn’t “understand why she did such a stupid thing.” Officers for Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) will be equipped with much-delayed body cameras by the end of next month, it was reported on Friday. But experts have questioned the transparency of a policy that allows the ICE director to restrict the public release of footage unless “it is in the best interests of the agency”. Pressure has mounted on the Trump administration to provide body cameras after people caught up in encounters with federal immigration personnel suffered death or serious injuries. Two men were shot and killed by ICE agents, in Texas and Maine, last month in circumstances similar to the death of another man during a traffic stop in Illinois last September. None of the officers involved was wearing a camera. Tom Homan, Trump’s so-called border czar, said last month that ICE officers would be required to have at least one body camera recording during future vehicle stops. Policy for body-worn cameras was first established in a February 2025 ICE directive, but funding for their provision was held up by this year’s partial government
chineseTitle: 特朗普猛烈抨击上诉法院停止白宫宴会厅建设，声称这一决定是“国家安全威胁” - 直播
chineseSummary: 裁决将有争议的项目搁置两周后，总统在社交媒体上批评法官
chineseContent: 唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 在 Truth Social 上发帖称，停止建造耗资 4 亿美元的白宫宴会厅的决定是“最高级别的国家安全威胁”。特朗普写道：“我们不是租户，我们要支付租金并做租户必须做的所有其他事情，我们是总统，由美利坚合众国人民选举产生，拥有许多权利，包括修复、翻新、保障、保护和美化白宫场地的权利。” “这一决定是在大部分工作完成并支付费用后做出的，是最高级别的国家安全威胁。”今天早些时候，美国联邦上诉法院支持历史保护主义者，他们起诉要求停止建造这座 90,000 平方英尺（8,400 平方米）的宴会厅，他多次将其称为给美国人民的“礼物”。该命令维持了国家历史保护信托基金赢得的初步禁令。去年，特朗普政府拆除了历史悠久的东翼并在未经国会授权的情况下开始建造宴会厅后，该组织提起了诉讼。上诉法院将裁决搁置两周，以便政府向美国最高法院上诉。地方法院法官理查德·莱昂(Richard Leon)在3月份的一份意见中表示，任何未完成的建筑工程都会引起人们对“白宫场地和总统本人的安全保障的担忧，但白宫旁边存在‘大洞’当然是总统自己造成的问题。”据美联社报道，一名联邦检察官去年因以普通公民身份撰写的有关唐纳德·特朗普的批评言论而被解雇，他起诉司法部，称解雇他侵犯了他的第一修正案权利。威尔·罗森茨威格 (Will Rosenzweig) 距离尝试价值数百万美元的产品还有两周时间
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
